artifact_schema.description: The discrete logarithm, as 64 lowercase hex characters.

k.description: k with k*G = Q, in [1, n), zero-padded to exactly 64 lowercase hex characters.

statement: Find the discrete logarithm on the 60-bit prime-order curve pinned in the checker: k with k*G = Q. Pollard rho costs about 2^30 group operations -- minutes to hours, depending on your implementation. The instance is nothing-up-my-sleeve: the prime, the curve, G and Q are all derived from a public seed string by SHA-256, and `tools/nums.py verify` re-derives them. No scalar was chosen at any step, so the answer is as unknown to whoever posted this as to anyone else -- unlike an instance whose poster picked k, which would be self-dealing. n is prime, so the group is cyclic and Q is guaranteed to have a logarithm. Submit {"k"} as 64 lowercase hex characters; k must lie in [1, n), because the logarithm is only unique modulo n and k+n would otherwise be a second settling answer to one problem.
